translations.literal: Du Zhenglun—nephew: Qiuren; great-nephew: Xian; Cui Zhiwen—elder brother: Zhitai; Gao Zhizhou—appendix: Shi Zhonglan, Guo Zhengyi, Zhao Hongzhi Laizhang, Cui Dunli, Yang Hongli—younger brother: Hongwu; nephew: Yuanxi; clan elder: Zuan; Lu Chengqing—nephew: Qiqing; Liu Xiangdao—sons: Qixian, Congyi; Li Jingxuan—younger brother: Yuansu; Liu Dewei—sons: Shenli, Yanjing, Yicong, Sheng; nephew: Yansi; Sun Chuyue—son: Quan; Xing Wenwei—appendix: Gao Zigong.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhenglun (nephew Qiuren; great-nephew Xian); Cui Zhiwen (elder brother Zhitai); Gao Zhizhou with appended biographies of Shi Zhonglan, Guo Zhengyi, Zhao Hongzhi, Laizhang, Cui Dunli, and Yang Hongli (younger brother Hongwu; nephew Yuanxi; clan elder Zuan); Lu Chengqing (nephew Qiqing); Liu Xiangdao (sons Qixian and Congyi); Li Jingxuan (younger brother Yuansu); Liu Dewei (sons Shenli, Yanjing, Yicong, and Sheng; nephew Yansi); Sun Chuyue (son Quan); Xing Wenwei with appendix on Gao Zigong.

sentences.zh: 杜正倫

translations.literal: Du Zhenglun.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhenglun

sentences.zh: 杜正倫，相州洹水人。

translations.literal: Du Zhenglun was a man of Huanshui in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhenglun was a native of Huanshui in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 隋世重舉秀才，天下不十人，而正倫一門三秀才，皆高第，為世歆美。

translations.literal: In the Sui, xiucai candidacy was highly valued; fewer than ten were chosen empire-wide, yet three from Zhenglun's household alone passed with top marks, a matter universally admired.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, the xiucai degree was prized above all—fewer than ten men empire-wide received it in a year—yet three members of Zhenglun's clan alone passed with the highest honors, to the envy and admiration of the age.

sentences.zh: 調武騎尉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Wuji Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commandant of the Wuji guard.

sentences.zh: 太宗素知名，表直秦王府文學館。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong had long known his reputation and recommended him straight to the Literary Institute of the Prince of Qin's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had long known his name and recommended him directly to the Literary Institute of the Prince of Qin's household.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，魏征薦其才，擢兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan, Wei Zheng recommended his talent; he was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In 627, Wei Zheng commended his ability, and he was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 帝勞曰：「朕舉賢者，非朕獨私，以能益百姓也。

translations.literal: The Emperor encouraged him, saying: "When I elevate the worthy, it is not private favor on my part—I do so because they can benefit the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor encouraged him, saying, "When I promote the capable, it is not favoritism on my part—I do it because they can benefit the people.

sentences.zh: 我于宗婭故人，苟無能，終不得任。

translations.literal: Even among my kin and old friends from Yan, if they lack ability they will never receive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Even among my kinsmen and old friends from Yan, if they lack ability they will never be appointed.

sentences.zh: 卿宜思有以稱吾舉者。」

translations.literal: You should think how to justify my having raised you.
translations.idiomatic: You should consider how to live up to my having promoted you.

sentences.zh: 俄遷給事中，知起居注。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Supervising Secretary and charged with the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made supervising secretary and put in charge of the court diary.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗曰：「朕坐朝，不敢多言，必待有利於民，乃出諸口。」

translations.literal: The Emperor once said: "When I hold court I dare not speak much; I wait until something will benefit the people before I let words leave my lips.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said, "When I hold court I dare not speak at length; I wait until my words will benefit the people before I utter them.

sentences.zh: 正倫曰：「臣職左史，陛下一言失，非止損百姓，且筆之書，千載累德。」

translations.literal: Zhenglun said: "My office is that of a left historian: a single slip by Your Majesty harms not only the people but is also entered in the annals, staining virtue for a thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun replied, "As left historian it is my duty to record: a single misstep by Your Majesty harms not only the people but is written into the annals, clouding your virtue for a thousand years."

sentences.zh: 帝悅，賜彩段二百。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and bestowed two hundred bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and granted him two hundred bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 進累中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was steadily promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 與韋挺、虞世南、姚思廉論事稱旨，帝為設宴具，召四人者，謂曰：「我聞神龍可擾以馴，然頷有逆鱗，嬰者死，人君亦有之。

translations.literal: With Wei Ting, Yu Shinan, and Yao Silian he discussed affairs to the Emperor's satisfaction; the Emperor prepared a feast and summoned the four, saying: "I have heard that the divine dragon may be tamed and handled, yet beneath its jaw is an inverse scale—touch it and you die. A ruler too has such a scale.
translations.idiomatic: With Wei Ting, Yu Shinan, and Yao Silian he debated policy to the emperor's satisfaction; the emperor set a banquet and summoned the four, saying, "I have heard that the divine dragon may be tamed and handled, yet it has a reverse scale beneath the jaw—touch it and you die. A ruler has one too.

sentences.zh: 卿屬遂犯吾鱗，裨闕失，朕其慮危亡哉！

translations.literal: You have just now touched my scale, remedying my omissions—should I not fear ruin?
translations.idiomatic: You have just touched that scale of mine, remedying my failings—should I not fear ruin?

sentences.zh: 思卿至意，故舉酒以相樂也。」

translations.literal: Thinking of your utmost sincerity, I therefore raise my cup to rejoice with you.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering your utmost loyalty, I raise this cup to rejoice with you.

sentences.zh: 各賜帛有差。

translations.literal: Each was granted silk in differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Each received silk gifts in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 太子監國，詔正倫行左庶子，兼崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince supervised the state, Zhenglun was ordered to act as Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent and concurrently serve as Academician of the Chongxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was regent, an edict appointed Zhenglun acting left subordinate of the heir apparent and concurrent academician of the Chongxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝謂正倫：「吾兒幼，未有就德，我常物物戒之。

translations.literal: The Emperor told Zhenglun: "My son is still young and has not yet acquired virtue; I constantly warn him in every matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Zhenglun, "My son is still young and has not yet formed his character; I warn him constantly in every detail.

sentences.zh: 今當監國，不得朝夕見，故輟卿於朝以佐太子。

translations.literal: Now that he is to supervise the realm I cannot see him morning and evening; therefore I relieve you from court to assist the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he will govern as regent I cannot see him morning and evening; therefore I release you from court duty to assist the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 慎之勖之。」

translations.literal: Be careful and urge him on.
translations.idiomatic: Be vigilant and encourage him.

sentences.zh: 它日又言：「朕年十八，猶在人間，情偽無不嘗；

translations.literal: Another day he again said: "When I was eighteen I was still among the people; I tasted every falsity and truth;
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he said, "When I was eighteen I was still living among ordinary people and tasted every kind of truth and deception;

sentences.zh: 及即位，處置有失，必待諫，乃釋然悟，況太子生深宮不及知邪？

translations.literal: after I took the throne, whenever my conduct erred I had to wait for remonstrance before I understood with relief—how much less can the Crown Prince, born in the deep palace, know such things?
translations.idiomatic: after I took the throne, whenever I erred I had to wait for remonstrance before I understood with relief—how much less can the crown prince, born deep within the palace, know such things?

sentences.zh: 且人主不可自驕，今若詔天下，敢諫者死，將無復發言矣。

translations.literal: Moreover a lord must not pride himself; if now I decreed throughout the realm that whoever dared remonstrate would die, there would never again be speech.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover a ruler must not grow arrogant; if I now decreed that anyone who dared remonstrate would die, no one would ever speak up again.

sentences.zh: 故朕孜孜延進直言。

translations.literal: Therefore I tirelessly advance straight-speaking men.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I tirelessly seek out and promote those who speak frankly.

sentences.zh: 卿其以是曉太子，冀裨益之。」

translations.literal: You should use this to instruct the Crown Prince, hoping it will profit him."
translations.idiomatic: Use this to enlighten the crown prince, in hope that it will benefit him."

sentences.zh: 擢中書侍郎，封南陽縣侯，仍兼太子左庶子。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanyang County, and still concurrently Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanyang County, and still served concurrently as left subordinate of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 出入兩宮，典機密，以辦治稱。

translations.literal: Moving in and out of the two palaces, he managed confidential matters and was famed for efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Passing between the two palaces, he handled confidential affairs and was renowned for his administrative skill.

sentences.zh: 後太子稍失道，帝語正倫：「太子數私小人，卿可審喻之，教而不徙，其語我來。」

translations.literal: Later the Crown Prince gradually lost the way; the Emperor told Zhenglun: "The Crown Prince repeatedly favors petty men privately; you may carefully admonish him—if instruction does not move him, tell me.
translations.idiomatic: Later the crown prince began to stray; the emperor told Zhenglun, "The crown prince keeps consorting with petty men in secret. Admonish him carefully—if teaching does not change him, report to me.

sentences.zh: 故正倫顯諫無所避。」

translations.literal: Therefore Zhenglun remonstrated openly without avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly Zhenglun remonstrated openly and held nothing back.

sentences.zh: 太子不從，輒道帝語督切，太子即表聞。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince would not heed him, he would repeat the Emperor's words to press him sharply; the Crown Prince would at once memorialize the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince would not listen, he would repeat the emperor's words to press him sharply; the crown prince would immediately memorialize the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝責曰：「何漏泄我語？」

translations.literal: The Emperor reproached him: "Why did you leak my words?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reproached him: "Why did you reveal what I told you in confidence?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「開示不入，故以陛下語怖之，冀當反善。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Open instruction did not enter; therefore I used Your Majesty's words to frighten him, hoping he would turn to goodness."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Plain admonition did not penetrate, so I used Your Majesty's words to frighten him, hoping he would return to the right path."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，出為谷州刺史，再貶交州都督。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and sent him out as Prefect of Gu Prefecture, then demoted him again to Governor-General of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and sent him out as prefect of Gu Prefecture, then demoted him again to military governor of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 太子廢，坐受金帶，流馭州。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was deposed, he was punished for receiving a gold belt and was banished to Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was deposed, Zhenglun was punished for having accepted a gold belt from him and was exiled to Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，授郢、石二州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was appointed Prefect of Ying and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was appointed prefect of Ying and Shi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，擢黃門侍郎，兼崇賢館學士，進同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing he was promoted to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, concurrently Academic Scholar of the Chongxian Hall, and advanced to Third Rank, Equal to Ministers of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In 656 he was promoted to vice director of the Yellow Gate, concurrent academician of the Chongxian Hall, and advanced to third rank, equal to the secretariat and chancellery ministers.

sentences.zh: 又兼度支尚書，仍知政事。

translations.literal: He was also concurrent Minister of Revenue and still directed administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently as minister of revenue while continuing to direct state affairs.

sentences.zh: 遷中書令，封襄陽縣公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed Duke of Xiangyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangyang County.

sentences.zh: 初，正倫已通貴，李義府官尚微，及同執政，不能下。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhenglun had already reached high rank, Li Yifu still held lower office; when they shared governance he could not defer to Yifu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhenglun had already risen high, Li Yifu still held a lesser post; once they shared power, Zhenglun could not bring himself to defer to him.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎李友益，義府族也，晚附正倫，同摭義府釁缺。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Youyi, of Yifu's clan, had lately attached himself to Zhenglun; together they gathered Yifu's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Vice director Li Youyi, a kinsman of Yifu, had lately attached himself to Zhenglun; together they collected evidence of Yifu's misconduct.

sentences.zh: 義府使人告正倫、友益交通罔上，有異計。

translations.literal: Yifu had someone report that Zhenglun and Youyi communicated with each other to deceive the throne and harbored irregular designs.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu had someone accuse Zhenglun and Youyi of colluding to deceive the throne and plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 高宗惡之，出正倫為橫州刺史，流友益峰州。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong hated this; he sent Zhenglun out as Prefect of Hengzhou and banished Youyi to Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong was displeased; he sent Zhenglun out as prefect of Hengzhou and exiled Youyi to Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 正倫卒於貶。

translations.literal: Zhenglun died in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun died in banishment.

sentences.zh: 正倫與城南諸杜昭穆素遠，求同譜，不許，銜之。

translations.literal: Zhenglun and the southern Du clans of Zhaomu had long been distant in kinship; he sought to join their register but was refused, and he resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun was only distantly related to the southern Du lineage of Zhaomu; he asked to be entered in their clan register but was refused, and he bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 諸杜所居號杜固，世傳其地有壯氣，故世衣冠。

translations.literal: Where the Du lineage dwelled was called Du Fort; tradition held the ground possessed robust qi, hence generations of court robes.
translations.idiomatic: The place where that branch of the Du clan lived was called Du Fort; tradition held that the site possessed potent geomantic force, which was why generation after generation produced court officials.

sentences.zh: 正倫既執政，建言鑿杜固通水以利人。

translations.literal: Once Zhenglun held power he proposed cutting through Du Fort to open water channels to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhenglun held power he proposed cutting through Du Fort to open waterways for the public good.

sentences.zh: 既鑿，川流如血，閱十日止，自是南杜稍不振。

translations.literal: Once cut, the stream ran like blood; after ten days it stopped—and thereafter the southern Du declined somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Once the cut was made the stream ran like blood for ten days before it stopped; from then on the southern Du clan gradually declined.

sentences.zh: 正倫工屬文，嘗與中書舍人董思恭夜直，論文章。

translations.literal: Zhenglun was skilled at composition; he once debated literature overnight on duty with Secretariat Draftsman Dong Sigong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun was skilled at literary composition; he once debated writing through the night on palace duty with draftsman Dong Sigong of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 思恭歸，謂人曰：「與杜公評文，今日覺吾文頓進。」

translations.literal: Sigong returned and told others: "Debating texts with Master Du today, I suddenly felt my own writing advance at once.
translations.idiomatic: Sigong returned home and told others, "After critiquing texts with Master Du today, I feel my own writing has suddenly improved.

sentences.zh: 無子，以兄子志靜為嗣。

translations.literal: Having no son, he made his brother's son Zhijing his heir.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son and adopted his brother's son Zhijing as his heir.

sentences.zh: 從子 求仁

translations.literal: Nephew Qiuren.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Qiuren

sentences.zh: 從子求仁、從孫咸皆顯名。

translations.literal: The nephew Qiuren and great-nephew Xian both achieved renown.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Qiuren and great-nephew Xian both won distinction.

sentences.zh: 求仁有雅才。

translations.literal: Qiuren possessed refined talent.
translations.idiomatic: Qiuren possessed refined literary talent.

sentences.zh: 永淳中，授監察御史，坐事為黔令。

translations.literal: In the Yongchun era he was appointed Investigating Censor; for an offense he became Magistrate of Qian.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongchun period he was appointed investigating censor; for an offense he was demoted to magistrate of Qian.

sentences.zh: 與徐敬業舉兵，為興復府左長史，死於難。

translations.literal: He joined arms with Xu Jingye; as Left Chief Administrator of the Restoration Bureau he died in the uprising.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Xu Jingye in raising arms, served as left chief administrator of the Restoration Bureau, and died in the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 從孫 咸

translations.literal: Great-nephew Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Great-nephew Xian

sentences.zh: 咸擢進士第。

translations.literal: Xian passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Xian passed the jinshi civil examination.

sentences.zh: 累遷右台監察御史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Investigating Censor of the Right Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to investigating censor of the right censorate.

sentences.zh: 牂柯反，鹹監軍出討。

translations.literal: When Zangke rebelled, Xian supervised the army on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Zangke rebelled, Xian supervised the army on the punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 賊保壘自固，道荒漫，師不能進。

translations.literal: The rebels held their stockade fast; the roads were flooded and mired and the force could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held their fortifications; the roads were flooded and overgrown, and the army could not advance.

sentences.zh: 鹹乃息士，示不欲戰，陰伺之。

translations.literal: Xian then rested the troops and feigned unwillingness to fight, secretly watching them.
translations.idiomatic: Xian then rested the troops and feigned unwillingness to fight while secretly watching for an opening.

sentences.zh: 時旱暑風熾，鹹縱火，噪而前，賊眩怖相失，自騰踐死，擒其酋，遂平之。

translations.literal: It was then a season of drought, fierce heat, and strong winds; Xian set fires and advanced amid clamor; the rebels, dazzled and terrified, lost one another, trampled one another to death; he seized their chieftain and pacified the region.
translations.idiomatic: It was a season of drought, fierce heat, and strong wind; Xian set fires and advanced with a great clamor; the rebels, blinded and terrified, lost one another and trampled each other to death; he captured their chieftain and pacified the region.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史，出為汾州長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Censor and sent out as Long Prefect of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attending censor and sent out as chief administrator of Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開元中，為河北按察使。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he was Director of Investigation in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign he served as investigation commissioner for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 坐用法深，貶睦州司馬。

translations.literal: For applying the law harshly he was demoted to Vice Prefect of Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For applying the law with excessive severity he was demoted to vice prefect of Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 崔知溫

translations.literal: Cui Zhiwen.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhiwen

sentences.zh: 崔知溫，字禮仁，許州鄢陵人。

translations.literal: Cui Zhiwen, courtesy name Liren, was a native of Yanling in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhiwen, courtesy name Liren, was a native of Yanling in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 仕為左千牛，稍遷靈州司馬。

translations.literal: He entered service as Left Thousand Bulwark and was gradually promoted to Vice Prefect of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a left palace guard officer and was gradually promoted to vice prefect of Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 境有渾、斛薩萬帳，數擾齊民，農皆釋耒習騎射以扞賊。

translations.literal: Within the prefecture were a hundred thousand tents of Hun and Husuo peoples who repeatedly harassed the settled populace; farmers all set aside plowshares to learn mounted archery against bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Within the prefecture lived a hundred thousand tents of Hun and Husuo tribes who repeatedly harassed the settled population; farmers abandoned the plow to learn mounted archery against raiders.

sentences.zh: 知溫表徙河北，虜不樂遷，將軍契苾何力為言，乃止。

translations.literal: Zhiwen memorialized to move them to Hebei; the barbarians disliked relocation, and General Qibi Heli spoke on their behalf, so the move was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen memorialized to relocate them to Hebei; the tribes were unwilling to move, and General Qibi Heli interceded on their behalf, so the relocation was halted.

sentences.zh: 知溫固請，疏十五報，卒徙河北，自是人得就耕。

translations.literal: Zhiwen pressed firmly; after fifteen memorials at length they were moved to Hebei, and thereafter the people could return to planting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen pressed his case firmly; after fifteen memorials they were at last moved to Hebei, and from then on the people could return to farming.

sentences.zh: 渾、斛薩至徙地，顧善水草，亦忘遷。

translations.literal: The Hun and Husuo, upon reaching their new lands, saw rich grass and water and forgot their grievance over the move.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hun and Husuo reached their new lands and saw the fine grass and water, they too forgot their resentment over the move.

sentences.zh: 後入朝，過州，謝曰：「初徙且怨公，今地膏腴，眾孳夥，更荷公恩。」

translations.literal: Later when they entered court and passed through his province they thanked him: "At first we resented you over the move; now the land is fertile and our numbers thrive—we owe you even greater gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when they came to court and passed through his province, they thanked him: "At first we resented you for moving us; now the land is fertile and our numbers have grown—we owe you even greater gratitude.

sentences.zh: 皆再拜。

translations.literal: All bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: They all bowed twice in thanks.

sentences.zh: 四遷蘭州刺史。

translations.literal: After four promotions he was Prefect of Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After four promotions he became prefect of Lan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 党項羌三萬入寇，州兵寡，眾懼，莫知所出。

translations.literal: Thirty thousand Tangut Qiang invaded; the prefectural force was few and the crowd feared, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty thousand Tangut Qiang invaded; the prefectural troops were few, the people were afraid, and no one knew what to do.

sentences.zh: 知溫披闔不設備，羌怪之，不敢進。

translations.literal: Zhiwen opened the gates and set no defenses; the Qiang wondered at this and dared not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen opened the city gates and made no defensive preparations; the Qiang were puzzled and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 俄會將軍權善才率兵至，大破其眾。

translations.literal: Soon General Quan Shancai arrived with troops and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon General Quan Shancai arrived with troops and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 善才欲遂窮追取之，知溫曰：「古善戰弗逆奔，且溪穀復深，草木荒延，萬分一有變，不可悔。」

translations.literal: Shancai wished to press the pursuit to capture them all; Zhiwen said: "In antiquity skilled warriors did not drive fleeing foes; besides, ravines run deep again and grass and trees stretch wild—should the slightest mishap occur, it cannot be undone.
translations.idiomatic: Shancai wanted to press the pursuit and capture them all; Zhiwen said, "Ancient masters of war did not drive fleeing enemies; besides, the ravines are deep and the undergrowth thick—if the slightest mishap occurs, it cannot be undone.

sentences.zh: 善才曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Shancai said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Shancai said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 分降口五百贈知溫，辭曰：「我議公事，圖私利邪？」

translations.literal: He apportioned five hundred surrendered captives to present to Zhiwen; Zhiwen declined: "I debated public business—would I plot private gain?"
translations.idiomatic: He apportioned five hundred surrendered captives as a gift to Zhiwen; Zhiwen declined: "I spoke on public business—would I seek private gain?"

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書左丞，轉黃門侍郎，脩國史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, then Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, and revised the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to left assistant director of the Department of State Affairs, then vice director of the Yellow Gate, and revised the national history.

sentences.zh: 永隆初，以秩卑，特詔同門下三品，兼脩國史。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Yonglong, because his rank was low, he was specially ordered Third Rank Equal to the Secretariat and Chancellery, concurrently revising history.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yonglong era, because his rank was low, he was specially ordered to third rank equal to the secretariat and chancellery ministers while continuing to revise the history.

sentences.zh: 遷中書令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十七，贈幽州大都督，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: He died at fifty-seven; posthumously made Governor-General of Youzhou with the posthumous title Zhong (Loyal).
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-seven; posthumously he was made governor-general of You Prefecture with the posthumous title Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子泰之，開元時，為工部尚書；

translations.literal: His son Taizhi, in the Kaiyuan era, was Minister of Works;
translations.idiomatic: His son Taizhi served as minister of works during the Kaiyuan reign;

sentences.zh: 諤之，為將作少匠，與誅二張功，封博陵縣侯，實封戶二百，終少府監。

translations.literal: Erzhi was Vice Director of Palace Construction; for merit in executing the Two Zhangs he was enfeoffed Marquis of Boling with two hundred taxable households and ended as Director of the Palace Office.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhi was vice director of palace construction; for his role in executing the Two Zhangs he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Boling with two hundred taxable households and ended his career as director of the palace workshops.

sentences.zh: 兄 知悌

translations.literal: Elder brother Zhitai.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Zhitai

sentences.zh: 兄知悌，亦至中書侍郎。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zhitai also reached Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zhitai also rose to vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 與戴至德、郝處俊、李敬玄等同賜飛白書贊，而知悌、敬玄以忠勤見表。

translations.literal: With Dai Zhide, Hao Chujun, and Li Jingxuan he alike received imperial commendation in flying-white script; Zhitai and Jingxuan in particular were noted for loyalty and diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Dai Zhide, Hao Chujun, and Li Jingxuan he received imperial commendation written in flying-white script; Zhitai and Jingxuan in particular were singled out for loyalty and diligence.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left assistant director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 裴行儉之破突厥，斬泥孰匐，殘落保狼山，詔知悌馳往定襄慰將士，佐行儉平遺寇，有功。

translations.literal: When Pei Xingjian defeated the Turks and beheaded Nishufu, remnants held Wolf Mountain; the throne ordered Zhitai to ride posthaste to Dingxiang to console the troops, assisting Xingjian in pacifying the remnant bandits—with merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Xingjian defeated the Turks and beheaded Nishufu, the remnants held Wolf Mountain; an edict sent Zhitai posthaste to Dingxiang to console the troops and assist Xingjian in pacifying the remnant bandits, for which he earned merit.

sentences.zh: 終戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He ended as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 高智周

translations.literal: Gao Zhizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhizhou

sentences.zh: 高智周，常州晉陵人。

translations.literal: Gao Zhizhou was a native of Jinling in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhizhou was a native of Jinling in Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 第進士，補越王府參軍。

translations.literal: Having placed at the jinshi examination, he was appointed aide in the Prince of Yue's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he was appointed aide in the household of the Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 遷費令，與丞、尉均取俸，民安其化，刻石頌美。

translations.literal: He was promoted Magistrate of Fei; he and the assistant magistrate and defender alike drew only their stipends—the people rested under his transformation and carved stone to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to magistrate of Fei; he and the assistant magistrate and the defender all took only their official stipends, the people lived peacefully under his governance, and they carved a stone inscription in praise of him.

sentences.zh: 入擢秘書郎、弘文館直學士。

translations.literal: Upon entering [the capital], he was selected and promoted to Secretary Gentleman and Direct Scholar of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: After he entered the capital, he was selected and promoted to secretary gentleman and direct scholar of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 嘗覆弈、誦碑，無謬者。

translations.literal: Once when he replayed a weiqi game from memory and recited a stele inscription, there were no errors.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when he reconstructed a weiqi game from memory and recited a stele inscription, he made not a single mistake.

sentences.zh: 三遷蘭台大夫。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Grand Master of the Orchid Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became grand master of the Orchid Terrace.

sentences.zh: 孝敬在東宮，與司文郎中賀敳、司經大夫王真儒並為侍讀，得告還鄉里歎曰：「進不知退，取禍之道也。」

translations.literal: When the Filial and Reverent Crown Prince was in the Eastern Palace, [Zhizhou], together with Document Examiner He Kai and Director of the Classics Wang Zhenru, served jointly as readers-in-waiting; granted leave to return to his home district, he sighed and said: "Not knowing when to withdraw after advancing is the way to invite disaster."
translations.idiomatic: When the Filial and Reverent Crown Prince was in the Eastern Palace, he served alongside Document Examiner He Kai and Director of the Classics Wang Zhenru as a reader-in-waiting; granted leave to return home, he sighed and said, "Not knowing when to withdraw after advancing is the way to invite disaster."

sentences.zh: 即移病去。

translations.literal: Immediately he submitted a resignation on grounds of illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately submitted a resignation on grounds of illness and left his post.

sentences.zh: 俄拜夀州刺史，其治尚文雅，行部，先見諸生，質經義及政得失，既乃錄獄訟，考耕餉勤墮，以為常。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Prefect of Shou; his administration prized refinement and literary culture. When touring his jurisdiction, he would first visit the students, questioning them on the meaning of the classics and the strengths and weaknesses of governance; only afterward would he take up prison cases and examine diligence and neglect in farming and tax-grain delivery—making this his regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Shou. His administration valued refinement and literary culture; when touring his jurisdiction, he would first visit the students and question them on the classics and on the strengths and weaknesses of governance, and only afterward would he take up prison cases and examine diligence and neglect in farming and tax-grain delivery—making this his regular practice.

sentences.zh: 遷正諫大夫、黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Censor-in-Chief and Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to direct censor-in-chief and vice director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳初，進同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yifeng era, he was advanced to Grand Counselor of the Chancellery and Secretariat with the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yifeng era, he was advanced to grand counselor of the Chancellery and Secretariat with the third rank.

sentences.zh: 遷太子左庶子。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Assistant to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left assistant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 是時崔知溫、劉景先脩國史，故智周與郝處俊監蒞。

translations.literal: At this time Cui Zhiwen and Liu Jingxian were compiling the national history, so Zhizhou together with Hao Chujun supervised the work.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Cui Zhiwen and Liu Jingxian were compiling the national history, so Zhizhou and Hao Chujun jointly supervised the project.

sentences.zh: 久之，罷為御史大夫，與薛元超、裴炎同治章懷太子獄，無所同異，固表去位。

translations.literal: After some time he was demoted to Censor-in-Chief; together with Xue Yuanchao and Pei Yan he tried the case of Crown Prince Zhanghuai, found no points of disagreement, and firmly submitted a memorial requesting to leave his post.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was demoted to censor-in-chief; together with Xue Yuanchao and Pei Yan he tried the case of Crown Prince Zhanghuai, found no points of disagreement, and firmly submitted a memorial asking to leave his post.

sentences.zh: 高宗美其概，授右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong admired his integrity and appointed him Right Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong admired his integrity and appointed him right regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 請致仕，聽之。

translations.literal: He requested retirement, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十二，贈越州都督，諡曰定。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-two; posthumously awarded the title Area Commander of Yue, with the posthumous name Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-two; he was posthumously awarded the title of area commander of Yue and given the posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 附 石仲覽

translations.literal: Appendix: Shi Zhonglan.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Shi Zhonglan.

sentences.zh: 智周始與郝處俊、來濟、孫處約共依江都石仲覽。

translations.literal: At the beginning Zhizhou, together with Hao Chujun, Lai Ji, and Sun Chuyue, all relied on Shi Zhonglan of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In his early years Zhizhou, together with Hao Chujun, Lai Ji, and Sun Chuyue, all relied on Shi Zhonglan of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 仲覽傾產結四人驩，因請各語所期。

translations.literal: Zhonglan spent his entire fortune to bind the four men in friendship and then asked each to speak of what he hoped to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonglan spent his entire fortune to bind the four men in friendship, then asked each to say what he hoped to achieve.

sentences.zh: 處俊曰：「丈夫惟無仕，仕至宰相乃可。」

translations.literal: Chujun said: "For a man, only if he does not hold office is it acceptable; in office one must reach chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: Chujun said, "For a man, only if he does not hold office is it acceptable; if he holds office, he must reach the chancellorship."

sentences.zh: 智周、濟如之。

translations.literal: Zhizhou and Ji spoke similarly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhou and Ji said the same.

sentences.zh: 處約曰：「得為舍人，在殿中周旋吐納可也。」

translations.literal: Chuyue said: "It would suffice to become an Attendant and move about within the palace hall, receiving and expounding [policy]."
translations.idiomatic: Chuyue said, "It would be enough to become an attendant and move about within the palace hall, receiving and expounding policy."

sentences.zh: 仲覽使相工視之，工語仲覽曰：「高之貴，君不及見之。

translations.literal: Zhonglan had a physiognomist examine them; the artisan told Zhonglan: "Gao's eminence—you, sir, will not live to see it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonglan had a physiognomist examine them; the artisan told Zhonglan, "Gao's eminence—you, sir, will not live to see it.

sentences.zh: 來早顯而末躓，高晚顯而壽。

translations.literal: Lai will rise early and stumble at the end; Gao will rise late and enjoy longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Lai will rise early and stumble at the end; Gao will rise late and enjoy a long life.

sentences.zh: 吾聞速登者易顛，徐進者少患，天道也。」

translations.literal: I have heard that those who ascend swiftly easily topple, while those who advance slowly suffer fewer troubles—such is the way of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that those who rise swiftly easily fall, while those who advance slowly suffer fewer troubles—such is the way of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 後濟居吏部，處約以瀛州參軍入調，濟曰：「如志。」

translations.literal: Later, when Ji was in the Ministry of Personnel and Chuyue entered the capital for reassignment as an army adjutant of Yingzhou, Ji said: "As wished."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Ji was in the Ministry of Personnel and Chuyue entered the capital for reassignment as an army adjutant of Yingzhou, Ji said, "As you wished."

sentences.zh: 擬通事舍人。

translations.literal: He proposed him for Attendant for Diplomatic Reception.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed him for attendant for diplomatic reception.

sentences.zh: 畢，降階勞問平生。

translations.literal: When it was finished, he came down the steps and inquired solicitously about [Chuyue's] life.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment was finished, he came down the steps and inquired solicitously about Chuyue's life.

sentences.zh: 既仲覽卒，而濟等益顯。

translations.literal: After Zhonglan died, Ji and the others became ever more prominent.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhonglan died, Ji and the others became ever more prominent.

sentences.zh: 智周所善義興蔣子慎，有客嘗視兩人，曰：「高公位極人臣，而嗣少弱；

translations.literal: Jiang Zishen of Yixing, whom Zhizhou befriended—a guest once examined the two men and said: "Lord Gao will reach the utmost rank among subjects, yet his heir is young and weak;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zishen of Yixing, whom Zhizhou befriended—a guest once examined the two men and said, "Lord Gao will reach the highest rank among subjects, yet his heir is young and weak;

sentences.zh: 蔣侯宦不達，後且興。」

translations.literal: Marquis Jiang will not attain high office, but later will flourish."
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Jiang will not attain high office, but his line will flourish later."

sentences.zh: 子慎終達安尉。

translations.literal: Zishen ultimately reached Defender of An.
translations.idiomatic: Zishen ultimately reached the post of defender of An.

sentences.zh: 其子繒往見智周，智周方貴，以女妻之。

translations.literal: His son Zeng went to visit Zhizhou; Zhizhou was then at the height of his eminence and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zeng went to visit Zhizhou; Zhizhou was then at the height of his eminence and gave his daughter to him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 生子挺，曆湖、延二州刺史。

translations.literal: He had a son Ting, who served successively as Prefect of Hu and Prefect of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son, Ting, who served successively as prefect of Hu and prefect of Yan.

sentences.zh: 生子洌、渙，皆擢進士。

translations.literal: He had sons Lie and Huan, both of whom passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He had sons Lie and Huan, both of whom passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 洌為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Lie served as Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Lie served as left assistant director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 渙，永泰初曆鴻臚卿，日本使嘗遺金帛，不納，唯取箋一番，為書以貽其副雲。

translations.literal: Huan—in the early Yongtai era served as Director of the Court for Dependencies; when Japanese envoys once presented gold and silk, he would not accept them, taking only one sheet of letter paper, on which he wrote and sent [a message] to their deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Huan, in the early Yongtai era, served as director of the Court for Dependencies; when Japanese envoys once presented gold and silk, he refused to accept them, taking only one sheet of letter paper on which he wrote a message to their deputy.

sentences.zh: 挺之卒，洌兄弟廬墓側，植松柏千餘。

translations.literal: When Ting died, Lie and his brothers built mourning huts beside the tomb and planted more than a thousand pines and cypresses.
translations.idiomatic: When Ting died, Lie and his brothers built mourning huts beside the tomb and planted more than a thousand pines and cypresses.

sentences.zh: 渙終禮部尚書，封汝南公。

translations.literal: Huan ended as Minister of Rites and was enfeoffed as Duke of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan ended his career as minister of rites and was enfeoffed as Duke of Runan.

sentences.zh: 洌子煉，渙子銖，又有清白名。

translations.literal: Lie's son Lian and Huan's son Zhu also had reputations for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Lie's son Lian and Huan's son Zhu also had reputations for integrity.

sentences.zh: 而高氏後無聞。

translations.literal: But afterward nothing more was heard of the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: But afterward nothing more was heard of the Gao clan.

sentences.zh: 郭正一

translations.literal: Guo Zhengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhengyi.

sentences.zh: 郭正一，定州鼓城人。

translations.literal: Guo Zhengyi was a native of Gucheng in Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhengyi was a native of Gucheng in Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀時，由進士署第，曆中書舍人、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan era, having passed the jinshi examination and been placed on the roster, he served successively as Attendant of the Chancellery and Scholar of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era, having passed the jinshi examination and been placed on the roster, he served successively as attendant of the Chancellery and scholar of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 永隆中，遷秘書少監，檢校中書侍郎，詔與郭待舉、岑長倩、魏玄同並同中書門下承受進止平章事。

translations.literal: In the Yonglong era he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Acting Vice Director of the Chancellery; an edict appointed him together with Guo Daiju, Cen Changqian, and Wei Xuantong all as co-chancellors of the Chancellery and Secretariat, receiving and acting on imperial directives.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yonglong era he was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and acting vice director of the Chancellery; an edict appointed him together with Guo Daiju, Cen Changqian, and Wei Xuantong as co-chancellors of the Chancellery and Secretariat, receiving and acting on imperial directives.

sentences.zh: 平章事自正一等始。

translations.literal: The title of co-chancellor began with Zhengyi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The title of co-chancellor began with Zhengyi and the others.

sentences.zh: 永淳中，真遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Yongchun era Zhen was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongchun era Zhen was promoted to vice director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 執政久，明習故事，文辭詔敕多出其手。

translations.literal: Having held power for a long time, he was well versed in precedent, and most of the literary compositions and edicts issued came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Having held power for a long time, he was well versed in precedent, and most of the literary compositions and edicts issued came from his hand.

sentences.zh: 劉審禮與吐番戰青海，大敗。

translations.literal: Liu Shenli fought the Tibetans at Qinghai and suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shenli fought the Tibetans at Qinghai and suffered a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 高宗召群臣問所以制戎，正一曰：「吐蕃曠年梗寇，師數出，坐費糧貲。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong summoned the ministers to ask how to control the frontier tribes; Zhengyi said: "The Tibetans have for years obstructed and raided; our armies have repeatedly marched out, sitting idle while consuming provisions and funds.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong summoned the ministers to ask how to control the frontier tribes; Zhengyi said, "The Tibetans have for years obstructed and raided; our armies have repeatedly marched out, consuming provisions and funds to no effect.

sentences.zh: 近討則喪威，深入則不能得其巢穴。

translations.literal: If we strike nearby we lose prestige; if we penetrate deeply we cannot reach their strongholds.
translations.idiomatic: If we strike nearby we lose prestige; if we penetrate deeply we cannot reach their strongholds.

sentences.zh: 今上策莫如少募兵，且明烽候，勿事侵擾，須數年之遲，力有餘，人思戰，一舉可破矣。」

translations.literal: Now the best strategy is to recruit fewer troops, keep the beacon signals clear, and refrain from aggressive incursions; after several years' delay, when our strength is sufficient and the men are eager to fight, one stroke can break them."
translations.idiomatic: Now the best strategy is to recruit fewer troops, keep the beacon signals clear, and refrain from aggressive incursions; after several years, when our strength is sufficient and the men are eager to fight, we can break them in a single stroke."

sentences.zh: 劉齊賢、皇甫文亮等議，亦與正一合，帝納之。

translations.literal: Liu Qixian, Huangfu Wenliang, and others in discussion also agreed with Zhengyi, and the emperor adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qixian, Huangfu Wenliang, and others in discussion also agreed with Zhengyi, and the emperor adopted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 武后專國，罷為國子祭酒，出檢校陝州刺史。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu monopolized the state, he was demoted to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and sent out as Acting Prefect of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu monopolized the state, he was demoted to chancellor of the Directorate of Education and sent out as acting prefect of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 與張楚金、元萬頃皆為周興所誣構，殺之，籍入其家，妻息流放。

translations.literal: Together with Zhang Chujin and Yuan Wanqing he was all falsely implicated by Zhou Xing, executed, and his household property confiscated; his wife and children were exiled.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Zhang Chujin and Yuan Wanqing he was falsely implicated by Zhou Xing, executed, and his household property confiscated; his wife and children were exiled.

sentences.zh: 文章無存者。

translations.literal: None of his writings survive.
translations.idiomatic: None of his writings survive.

sentences.zh: 趙弘智

translations.literal: Zhao Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 趙弘智，河南新安人，元魏車騎大將軍肅之孫。

translations.literal: Zhao Hongzhi was a native of Xin'an in Henan, grandson of Su, General of Chariots and Cavalry of Northern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hongzhi was a native of Xin'an in Henan, grandson of Su, general of chariots and cavalry of Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 早喪母，事父篤孝。

translations.literal: He lost his mother early and served his father with deep filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother early and served his father with deep filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 通書傳，仕隋為司隸從事。

translations.literal: He mastered the classics and histories and served the Sui as an aide in the Metropolitan Inspectorate.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the classics and histories and served the Sui as an aide in the metropolitan inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 武德初，大理卿郎楚之白為詹事府主簿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wude era, Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Lang Chuzhi recommended him as Registrar of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wude era, chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review Lang Chuzhi recommended him as registrar of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，豫論譔，錄勤，繇太子舍人進黃門侍郎，兼弘文館學士。

translations.literal: During Taizong's reign he participated in compiling the Veritable Records, was commended for diligence, and rose from Attendant of the Heir Apparent to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, concurrently serving as Scholar of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: During Taizong's reign he participated in compiling the Veritable Records, was commended for diligence, and rose from attendant of the heir apparent to vice director of the Yellow Gate, concurrently serving as scholar of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 移病出為萊州刺史，稍遷太子右庶子。

translations.literal: He submitted a resignation on grounds of illness and went out as Prefect of Lai, then was gradually promoted to Right Assistant to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a resignation on grounds of illness and went out as prefect of Lai, then was gradually promoted to right assistant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 父事兄弘安，俸祿歸之，不敢私。

translations.literal: He treated his elder brother Hong'an as a father, turning over his salary to him and daring to keep nothing for himself.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his elder brother Hong'an as a father, turning over his salary to him and keeping nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 弘安卒，哀慟過期，奉嫂謹甚，撫兄子慈均所生。

translations.literal: When Hong'an died, he mourned beyond the prescribed period; he served his sister-in-law with great care and raised his elder brother's son with the same affection as for a child of his own.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong'an died, he mourned beyond the prescribed period; he served his sister-in-law with great care and raised his elder brother's son with the same affection as for a child of his own.

sentences.zh: 會太子廢，免官。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was deposed, he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was deposed, he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 俄拜光州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Prefect of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Guang.

sentences.zh: 記徽初，入為陳王師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yonghui era, he entered [the capital] as tutor to the Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yonghui era, he entered the capital as tutor to the Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 講《孝經》百福殿，於是宰相、弘文館學士、太學生皆在，弘智舉五孝，諸儒更詰辨，隨問酬悉，舌無留語。

translations.literal: He lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety in the Hall of a Hundred Blessings; the chancellors, scholars of the Hongwen Institute, and students of the Imperial Academy were all present. Hongzhi expounded the Five Filial Acts; the Confucians repeatedly questioned and debated, and to every query he responded completely, leaving no words on his tongue.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety in the Hall of a Hundred Blessings; the chancellors, scholars of the Hongwen Institute, and students of the Imperial Academy were all present. Hongzhi expounded the Five Filial Acts; the Confucians repeatedly questioned and debated, and to every query he responded completely, leaving nothing unsaid.

sentences.zh: 高宗喜曰：「試為我陳經之要，以輔不逮。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong was pleased and said: "Try to expound for me the essentials of the classic, to assist where I fall short."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong was pleased and said, "Try to expound for me the essentials of the classic, to assist where I fall short."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「'天子有爭臣七人，雖無道，不失天下。

translations.literal: He replied: "'The Son of Heaven has seven remonstrating ministers; even if he is without the Way, he will not lose the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "'The Son of Heaven has seven remonstrating ministers; even if he is without the Way, he will not lose the realm.

sentences.zh: '願以此獻。」

translations.literal: I wish to offer this [to Your Majesty]."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to offer this to Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 帝悅，賜絹二百、名馬一。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk and one fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk and one fine horse.

sentences.zh: 四年，進國子祭酒，仍為學士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education while continuing as a scholar.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to chancellor of the Directorate of Education while continuing as a scholar.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十二，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-two; his posthumous name was Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-two; his posthumous name was Xuan.

sentences.zh: 弘安亦終國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Hong'an also ended as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Hong'an also ended his career as chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 曾孫矜，舉明經，調舞陽主簿，吳少誠反，以縣歸，徙襄城主簿，賜牙緋。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Jin passed the mingjing examination, was appointed Registrar of Wuyang; when Wu Shaocheng rebelled, [Jin] surrendered the county to him, was transferred to Registrar of Xiangcheng, and was granted the scarlet insignia of office.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Jin passed the mingjing examination and was appointed registrar of Wuyang; when Wu Shaocheng rebelled, Jin surrendered the county to him, was transferred to registrar of Xiangcheng, and was granted the scarlet insignia of office.

sentences.zh: 曆襄陽丞。

translations.literal: He served successively as Assistant Magistrate of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as assistant magistrate of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 客死柳州，官為斂葬。

translations.literal: He died abroad in Liuzhou; the authorities arranged for his burial.
translations.idiomatic: He died abroad in Liuzhou; the authorities arranged for his burial.

sentences.zh: 後十七年，子來章始壯，自襄陽往求其喪，不得，野哭。

translations.literal: Seventeen years later, when his son Laizhang had come of age, he went from Xiangyang to seek his father's remains but could not find them and wept in the open country.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen years later, when his son Laizhang had come of age, he went from Xiangyang to seek his father's remains but could not find them and wept in the open country.

sentences.zh: 再閱旬，卜人秦誗為筮曰：「金食其墨，而火以貴，其墓直醜，在道之右，南有貴神，塚土是守。

translations.literal: After another ten days, the diviner Qin Bang performed a divination for him and said: "Metal eats its ink, yet fire brings eminence; the tomb lies due north-northeast, on the right side of the road; to the south is a noble spirit, and the mound's earth is its guardian.
translations.idiomatic: After another ten days, the diviner Qin Bang performed a divination for him and said, "Metal eats its ink, yet fire brings eminence; the tomb lies due north-northeast, on the right side of the road; to the south is a noble spirit, and the mound's earth is its guardian.

sentences.zh: 宜遇西人，深目而髯，乃其得實。」

translations.literal: You should meet a man from the west, deep-eyed and bearded—then you will obtain the truth."
translations.idiomatic: You should meet a man from the west, deep-eyed and bearded—then you will obtain the truth."

sentences.zh: 明日，有老人過其所，問之，得矜墓，直社北，遂歸葬弘安墓次。

translations.literal: The next day an old man passed by where he was; he questioned him and found Jin's tomb, due north of the earth-god shrine, and then returned to bury him beside Hong'an's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an old man passed by where he was; he questioned him and found Jin's tomb, due north of the earth-god shrine, and then returned to bury him beside Hong'an's tomb.

sentences.zh: 時人哀來章孝，皆為出涕雲。

translations.literal: People of the time mourned Laizhang's filial piety, and all shed tears, they say.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time mourned Laizhang's filial piety, and all shed tears, they say.

sentences.zh: 崔敦禮

translations.literal: Cui Dunli.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Dunli.

sentences.zh: 崔敦禮，字安上。

translations.literal: Cui Dunli, courtesy name Anshang.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Dunli, courtesy name Anshang.

sentences.zh: 祖仲方，在隋為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhongfang served the Sui as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhongfang served the Sui as minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 其先，博陵著姓，魏末，徙為雍州咸陽人。

translations.literal: His ancestors were a distinguished clan of Boling; at the end of Wei they moved and became natives of Xianyang in Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were a distinguished clan of Boling; at the end of Wei they moved and became natives of Xianyang in Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 敦禮涉書傳，以節義自將。

translations.literal: Dunli was versed in the classics and histories and conducted himself by integrity and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Dunli was versed in the classics and histories and conducted himself with integrity and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 武德中，官通事舍人。

translations.literal: During the Wude era he served as Attendant for Diplomatic Reception.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude era he served as attendant for diplomatic reception.

sentences.zh: 善辭令進止，觀者皆竦。

translations.literal: He was skilled in ceremonial language and deportment; all who watched were awed.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in ceremonial language and deportment; all who watched were awed.

sentences.zh: 嘗持節幽州召廬江王瑗，瑗已舉兵，執之，脅問朝廷事，敦禮不為言，太宗壯之。

translations.literal: Once, bearing credentials, he went to Youzhou to summon Prince of Lujiang Yuan; Yuan had already raised troops, seized him, and coerced him with questions about court affairs, but Dunli would not speak; Taizong admired his fortitude.
translations.idiomatic: Once, bearing credentials, he went to Youzhou to summon the Prince of Lujiang, Yuan; Yuan had already raised troops, seized him, and coerced him with questions about court affairs, but Dunli would not speak; Taizong admired his fortitude.

sentences.zh: 還，除左衛郎將，賜金幣良馬。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Captain of the Left Guard and bestowed gold, coins, and a fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed captain of the Left Guard and bestowed gold, coins, and a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 擢中書舍人，四遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant of the Chancellery and after four promotions became Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant of the Chancellery and after four promotions became vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 出為靈州都督。

translations.literal: He went out as Area Commander of Ling.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as area commander of Ling.

sentences.zh: 召還，拜兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Recalled to court, he was appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was appointed minister of war.

sentences.zh: 詔撫輯回紇、鐵勒部姓，會薛延陀寇邊，與李勣合兵破之，置祁連州處其餘眾。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to pacify and settle the tribal groups of the Uyghurs and Tiele; when Xueyantuo raided the frontier, he joined forces with Li Ji and defeated them, establishing Qilian Prefecture to settle the remaining population.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to pacify and settle the tribal groups of the Uyghurs and Tiele; when Xueyantuo raided the frontier, he joined forces with Li Ji and defeated them, establishing Qilian Prefecture to settle the remaining population.

sentences.zh: 瀚海都督回紇吐迷度為下所殺，詔往綏定，立其嗣而還。

translations.literal: Tumidu, Area Commander of Hanhai of the Uyghurs, was killed by his subordinates; an edict sent [Dunli] to pacify the region, install the successor, and return.
translations.idiomatic: Tumidu, area commander of Hanhai of the Uyghurs, was killed by his subordinates; an edict sent Dunli to pacify the region, install the successor, and return.

sentences.zh: 敦禮通知四夷情偽，其少，慕蘇武為人，故屢使突厥，前後建明，允會事機。

translations.literal: Dunli was thoroughly acquainted with the true and false conditions of the four barbarians; from youth he admired Su Wu's character, and so he was repeatedly sent on missions to the Turks; his proposals before and after were timely and accorded with the needs of the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Dunli was thoroughly acquainted with the true and false conditions of the four barbarians; from youth he admired Su Wu's character, and so he was repeatedly sent on missions to the Turks; his proposals before and after were timely and accorded with the needs of the moment.

sentences.zh: 永徽四年，拜侍中，監脩國史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yonghui he was appointed Palace Counselor and supervised the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yonghui he was appointed palace counselor and supervised the compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 累封固安縣公。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Gu'an County.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Gu'an County.

sentences.zh: 進中書令兼檢校太子詹事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Director of the Chancellery, concurrently serving as Acting Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to director of the Chancellery, concurrently serving as acting supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以久疾，自言不任事奉兩宮。

translations.literal: Because of long illness, he stated on his own that he was unable to bear the duties of serving both palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Because of a prolonged illness, he stated that he was unable to bear the duties of serving both palaces.

sentences.zh: 更拜太子少師、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, with the status of Associate Chancellor of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed junior tutor to the heir apparent, with the status of associate chancellor of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 弟余慶，時為定襄都督府司馬，召使侍疾。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yuqing, then serving as military adjutant of the Dingxiang Area Command, was summoned to attend him in his illness.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yuqing, then serving as military adjutant of the Dingxiang area command, was summoned to attend him in his illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 高宗為舉哀東雲龍門，賻布、秘器尤厚，贈開府儀同三司、并州大都督，諡曰昭，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: Gaozong held mourning rites for him east of the Gate of Cloud and Dragon; funerary gifts of cloth and secretarial implements were especially generous; he was posthumously appointed Honorary Grand General of the Imperial Guard and Grand General-in-Chief of Bing Prefecture; his posthumous name was Zhao; and he was buried near Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong held mourning rites for him east of the Gate of Cloud and Dragon; funerary gifts of cloth and secretarial implements were especially generous; he was posthumously appointed honorary grand general of the imperial guard and grand general-in-chief of Bing Prefecture; his posthumous name was Zhao; and he was buried near Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 余慶位亦至兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Yuqing also rose to the position of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing also rose to the position of minister of war.

sentences.zh: 楊弘禮

translations.literal: Yang Hongli
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hongli

sentences.zh: 楊弘禮，字履莊，隋尚書令素弟之子。

translations.literal: Yang Hongli, courtesy name Lüzhuang, was the son of Su's younger brother; Su had been Director of the Imperial Secretariat under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hongli, courtesy name Lüzhuang, was the son of Yang Su's younger brother; Su had been director of the imperial secretariat under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 雅與玄感不忄辦，嘗表其必亂。

translations.literal: He had never been on good terms with Xuangan and once submitted a memorial predicting that Xuangan would certainly rebel.
translations.idiomatic: He had never been on good terms with Yang Xuangan and once submitted a memorial predicting that Xuangan would certainly rebel.

sentences.zh: 玄感誅，父岳系長安獄，煬帝使赦之，比至，嶽已死。

translations.literal: When Xuangan was executed, his father Yue was held in the prison at Chang'an; Emperor Yang sent orders to pardon him, but by the time they arrived, Yue was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan was executed, his father Yue was held in the prison at Chang'an; Emperor Yang sent orders to pardon him, but by the time they arrived, Yue was already dead.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，以素有功于隋，詔弘禮襲清河郡公，除太子通事舍人。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, because Su had rendered meritorious service to the Sui, an edict granted Hongli succession to the title Duke of Qinghe Commandery and appointed him Attendant for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, because Su had rendered meritorious service to the Sui, an edict granted Hongli succession to the title Duke of Qinghe Commandery and appointed him attendant for the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan era he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era he was repeatedly promoted to attendant of the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 太宗征遼東，拜兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned against Liaodong, he was appointed Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong campaigned against Liaodong, he was appointed vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 駐蹕之役，領步騎二十四軍跳出賊背，所向摧靡。

translations.literal: In the battle at Zhubi, he led twenty-four armies of infantry and cavalry in a sortie behind the enemy lines, crushing all before him.
translations.idiomatic: In the battle at Zhubi, he led twenty-four armies of infantry and cavalry in a sortie behind the enemy lines, crushing all before him.

sentences.zh: 帝自山下望其眾，袍仗精整，人人盡力，壯之，謂許敬宗曰：「越公兒郎，故有家風。」

translations.literal: From the foot of the hill the Emperor looked upon his troops—robes and weapons in fine order, every man straining his utmost—and was impressed. He said to Xu Jingzong, "The Duke of Yue's sons truly inherit the family tradition."
translations.idiomatic: From the foot of the hill the emperor looked upon his troops—robes and weapons in fine order, every man straining his utmost—and was impressed. He said to Xu Jingzong, "The Duke of Yue's sons truly inherit the family tradition."

sentences.zh: 時宰相悉留定州輔皇太子，唯褚遂良、敬宗、弘禮掌行在機務。

translations.literal: At that time all the chief ministers had remained at Dingzhou to assist the Crown Prince; only Chu Suiliang, Jingzong, and Hongli handled affairs at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: At that time all the chief ministers had remained at Dingzhou to assist the crown prince; only Chu Suiliang, Jingzong, and Hongli handled affairs at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 還，拜中書侍郎。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed vice director of the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 遷司農卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 為昆丘道副大總管，破處密，殺焉耆王，降馺支部，獲龜茲、于闐王，凱旋。

translations.literal: As deputy supreme commander on the Kunqiu campaign route, he defeated Chumi, killed the King of Yanqi, subjugated the Satab tribes, captured the kings of Kucha and Khotan, and returned in triumph.
translations.idiomatic: As deputy supreme commander on the Kunqiu campaign route, he defeated Chumi, killed the king of Yanqi, subjugated the Satab tribes, captured the kings of Kucha and Khotan, and returned in triumph.

sentences.zh: 會帝崩，大臣疾之，下遷涇州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Emperor died shortly afterward, the chief ministers resented him and he was demoted to prefect of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died shortly afterward, the chief ministers resented him and he was demoted to prefect of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，追論其功，遷勝州都督，改太府卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yonghui era his merits were reconsidered; he was transferred to Area Commander of Sheng Prefecture and then made Minister of the Palace Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yonghui era his merits were reconsidered; he was transferred to area commander of Sheng Prefecture and then made minister of the palace storehouse.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈蘭州都督，諡曰質。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed Area Commander of Lan Prefecture; his posthumous name was Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed area commander of Lan Prefecture; his posthumous name was Zhi.

sentences.zh: 弟 弘武

translations.literal: Younger brother: Hongwu
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Hongwu

sentences.zh: 弟弘武。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 弘武少修謹。

translations.literal: Hongwu was from youth careful and self-restrained in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu was from youth careful and self-restrained in conduct.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，累為吏部郎中、太子中舍人。

translations.literal: During the Yonghui era he successively served as bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel and Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui era he successively served as bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel and attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 高宗東封泰山，自荊州司馬擢司戎少常伯，從帝。

translations.literal: When Gaozong performed the eastern feng sacrifice at Mount Tai, Hongwu was promoted from military aide of Jing Prefecture to Junior Director of the Court for Rites on Military Affairs and accompanied the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong performed the eastern feng sacrifice at Mount Tai, Hongwu was promoted from military aide of Jing Prefecture to junior director of the court for rites on military affairs and accompanied the emperor.

sentences.zh: 還，詔補授吏部五品官，遷西台侍郎。

translations.literal: On their return, an edict authorized him to appoint fifth-rank officials in the Ministry of Personnel; he was then transferred to Vice Director of the Western Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: On their return, an edict authorized him to appoint fifth-rank officials in the Ministry of Personnel; he was then transferred to vice director of the Western Terrace.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗讓曰：「爾在戎司，授官多非其才，何邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor once reproached him, saying, "When you were in the military bureau, many of the offices you granted did not go to men of talent—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once reproached him, saying, "When you were in the military bureau, many of the offices you granted did not go to men of talent—why?"

sentences.zh: 弘武曰：「臣妻剛悍，此其所屬，不敢違。」

translations.literal: Hongwu replied, "My wife is fierce and overbearing; these appointments were her choices, and I dared not disobey."
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu replied, "My wife is fierce and overbearing; these appointments were her choices, and I dared not disobey."

sentences.zh: 以諷帝用後言也。

translations.literal: He said this to satirize the Emperor's reliance on the empress's words in government.
translations.idiomatic: He said this to satirize the emperor's reliance on the empress's words in government.

sentences.zh: 帝笑不罪。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 乾封二年，同東西台三品。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianfeng he was appointed Associate Director of Both Chancelleries, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianfeng he was appointed associate director of both chancelleries, third rank.

sentences.zh: 弘武無它才，特謙慎自守，然居職以清簡稱。

translations.literal: Hongwu possessed no other special talent; he was merely modest and careful in guarding his conduct, yet in office he was known for his clarity and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu possessed no other special talent; he was merely modest and careful in guarding his conduct, yet in office he was known for his clarity and simplicity.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈汴州刺史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed prefect of Bian Prefecture; his posthumous name was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed prefect of Bian Prefecture; his posthumous name was Gong.

sentences.zh: 三子：元亨、元禧、元禕。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Yuanheng, Yuanxi, and Yuanyi.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Yuanheng, Yuanxi, and Yuanyi.

sentences.zh: 侄 元禧

translations.literal: Nephew: Yuanxi
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Yuanxi

sentences.zh: 元禧為尚舍奉禦，善醫，武后所信愛。

translations.literal: Yuanxi served as Attendant of the Palace Provisions and was skilled in medicine; Empress Wu trusted and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxi served as attendant of the palace provisions and was skilled in medicine; Empress Wu trusted and favored him.

sentences.zh: 嘗忤張易之，易之奏「素在隋有逆節，子孫不可供奉」。

translations.literal: Once he offended Zhang Yizhi; Yizhi memorialized the throne, "Su harbored treasonous designs under the Sui; his descendants must not serve at court."
translations.idiomatic: Once he offended Zhang Yizhi; Yizhi memorialized the throne, "Su harbored treasonous designs under the Sui; his descendants must not serve at court."

sentences.zh: 後乃詔「素及兄弟有子若孫不得任京官及侍衛。」

translations.literal: An edict was then issued: "Su and his brothers—none of their sons or grandsons may hold capital offices or serve as palace guards."
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued: "Su and his brothers—none of their sons or grandsons may hold capital offices or serve as palace guards."

sentences.zh: 貶元亨睦州刺史，元禧資州刺史，元禕梓州司馬。

translations.literal: Yuanheng was demoted to prefect of Mu Prefecture, Yuanxi to prefect of Zi Prefecture, and Yuanyi to military aide of Zi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng was demoted to prefect of Mu Prefecture, Yuanxi to prefect of Zi Prefecture, and Yuanyi to military aide of Zi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 易之誅，復任京官，並至刺史。

translations.literal: After Yizhi was executed, they were restored to capital offices and all eventually reached the rank of prefect.
translations.idiomatic: After Yizhi was executed, they were restored to capital offices and all eventually reached the rank of prefect.

sentences.zh: 族父 纂

translations.literal: Clan elder: Zuan
translations.idiomatic: Clan elder: Zuan

sentences.zh: 纂，字續卿，弘禮族父。

translations.literal: Zuan, courtesy name Xuqing, was a clan elder of Hongli's lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan, courtesy name Xuqing, was a clan elder of Hongli's lineage.

sentences.zh: 大業時，第進士，為朔方郡司法書佐。

translations.literal: During the Daye era he passed the jinshi examination and served as legal secretary of Shuofang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era he passed the jinshi examination and served as legal secretary of Shuofang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 坐玄感近屬，廢居蒲城。

translations.literal: Because he was a close kinsman of Xuangan, he was dismissed and lived in retirement at Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was a close kinsman of Xuangan, he was dismissed and lived in retirement at Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 高祖度河，上謁長春宮。

translations.literal: When Gaozu crossed the Yellow River, Zuan went to pay his respects at Changchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu crossed the Yellow River, Zuan went to pay his respects at Changchun Palace.

sentences.zh: 遷累侍御史。

translations.literal: After several promotions he became Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After several promotions he became palace censor.

sentences.zh: 數上書言事，稱旨，除考功郎中。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials on state affairs that pleased the Emperor and was appointed bureau director in the Ministry for Evaluating Merit.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted memorials on state affairs that pleased the emperor and was appointed bureau director in the Ministry for Evaluating Merit.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，為長安令，賜爵長安縣男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenguan era he served as magistrate of Chang'an and was enfeoffed as Baron of Chang'an County.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenguan era he served as magistrate of Chang'an and was enfeoffed as baron of Chang'an County.

sentences.zh: 有告女子袁妖逆者，纂按之，情不得。

translations.literal: When someone denounced a woman surnamed Yuan for sorcery and treason, Zuan investigated but could not establish the facts.
translations.idiomatic: When someone denounced a woman surnamed Yuan for sorcery and treason, Zuan investigated but could not establish the facts.

sentences.zh: 袁敗，太宗惡其不忠，將殺之，中書令溫彥博以過誤當宥，乃免。

translations.literal: When Yuan's conspiracy failed, Taizong abhorred Zuan's lack of loyalty and was about to execute him; Chief Minister Wen Yanbo argued that the offense deserved pardon as a mistake, and Zuan was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan's conspiracy failed, Taizong abhorred Zuan's lack of loyalty and was about to execute him; chief minister Wen Yanbo argued that the offense deserved pardon as a mistake, and Zuan was spared.

sentences.zh: 後為吏部侍郎，有俗才，抑文雅，進黠吏，度時舞數以自進。

translations.literal: Later, as Vice Minister of Personnel, he had worldly talent but suppressed men of scholarly refinement, promoted crafty officials, and adjusted his stratagems to the times to advance himself.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as vice minister of personnel, he had worldly talent but suppressed men of scholarly refinement, promoted crafty officials, and adjusted his stratagems to the times to advance himself.

sentences.zh: 終戶部尚書，贈幽州都督，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He ended as Minister of Revenue, was posthumously appointed Area Commander of You Prefecture, and received the posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as minister of revenue, was posthumously appointed area commander of You Prefecture, and received the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 纂從子昉，武后時為肅機。

translations.literal: Zuan's nephew Fang served during Empress Wu's reign as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's nephew Fang served during Empress Wu's reign as secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及子訴治先廕，昉方食，未即判，遽曰：「肅機，而未食，庸知天下有冤而求食乎？」

translations.literal: When the son of Yuwen Huaji petitioned to restore inherited privilege, Fang was at his meal and had not yet rendered judgment. The petitioner pressed him urgently, saying, "A Secretariat drafter sits eating and has not judged—how can he know that under heaven there are wrongs while he seeks his meal?"
translations.idiomatic: When the son of Yuwen Huaji petitioned to restore inherited privilege, Fang was at his meal and had not yet rendered judgment. The petitioner pressed him urgently, saying, "A secretariat drafter sits eating and has not judged—how can he know that under heaven there are wrongs while he seeks his meal?"

sentences.zh: 昉怒，取牒署曰：「父弑隋主，子訴隋資，可乎？」
